:::{#def-observation-loss}
#### Loss of a prediction rule on an observation

The **loss** of a [prediction rule](#def-prediction-rule) $\fitted$ on an observation $(\predvar_{\iobs}, \outvar_{\iobs})$
is the cost, under a [loss function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-loss-function) $\loss$,
of its prediction $\fitted(\predvar_{\iobs})$ of the outcome $\outvar_{\iobs}$:

$$
\obsloss{\iobs} \eqdef \lossf{\outvar_{\iobs}, \fitted(\predvar_{\iobs})}.
$$ {#eq-observation-loss}

The index $*$ names the new observation $(\newpredvar, \newoutvar)$,
so $\obsloss{*} = \lossf{\newoutvar, \fitted(\newpredvar)}$.

:::
